questions.question: Which Gospel opens with the foundational declaration: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God'?
questions.explanation: St. John's prologue presents Christ as the eternal Logos ('Verbum') through whom all creation was made, inspiring the name Verbum Caro.

questions.question: How many canonical books are contained in the Catholic Old Testament, including the deuterocanonical texts?
questions.explanation: The Catholic Old Testament contains 46 books, preserving the 7 deuterocanonical books (Tobit, Judith, 1 & 2 Maccabees, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch) from the Greek Septuagint.

questions.question: Which Epistle emphasizes the unity of faith and action with the verse: 'So faith also, if it have not works, is dead in itself'?
questions.citation: James 2:17 (Vulgate: sic et fides, si non habeat opera, mortua est in semetipsa)
questions.explanation: St. James teaches that genuine Christian faith is not merely intellectual assent, but actively lives out charity through righteous works.

questions.question: Who was the devout elder in Jerusalem who took the infant Christ into his arms in the Temple and praised God with the 'Nunc Dimittis'?
questions.explanation: Simeon had been promised by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord's Messiah: 'Now dismiss thy servant, O Lord, according to thy word in peace.'

questions.question: Which prophet spoke the famous oracle: 'Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel'?
questions.explanation: The prophet Isaiah delivered this sign to the House of David, fulfilled in the Virgin Mary and the Incarnation of Jesus Christ.

questions.question: On which holy mountain did Moses receive the Tablets of the Ten Commandments from God?
questions.explanation: God made His covenant with the Israelites and handed down the Decalogue to Moses atop Mount Sinai.

questions.question: Which Psalm begins with the beloved verse: 'The Lord is my shepherd: and nothing shall be wanting to me'?
questions.citation: Psalm 22 in Vulgate / Psalm 23 in Hebrew numbering
questions.explanation: The pastoral Psalm of David expresses complete filial trust in God's providential care and guidance.

questions.question: In which garden did Jesus endure His agony in prayer the night before His crucifixion?
questions.explanation: At Gethsemane on the Mount of Olives, Jesus prayed: 'My Father, if it be possible, let this chalice pass from me. Nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.'

questions.question: On which feast day was the Holy Spirit poured out upon the Apostles in tongues as of fire?
questions.explanation: Fifty days after the Resurrection, on the Jewish feast of Pentecost (Shavuot), the Holy Spirit descended, marking the birth of the Church.

questions.question: Which early Church Father translated the Hebrew and Greek scriptures into Latin, producing the authoritative Latin Vulgate?
questions.citation: Catholic Church History / Council of Trent
questions.explanation: Commissioned by Pope Damasus I in 382 AD, St. Jerome spent decades in Bethlehem translating the Sacred Scriptures into Latin.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10), who was the first person to pass by the wounded traveler without assisting?
questions.explanation: A priest went down the same way and, seeing him, passed by; then a Levite similarly passed by before the Samaritan showed mercy.

questions.question: Which book of Wisdom begins with the famous passage: 'All things have their season, and in their times all things pass under heaven' ('A time to be born, and a time to die')?
questions.explanation: Written by Qoheleth, Ecclesiastes reflects on the seasons of human mortality and the sovereignty of God over time.

questions.question: What is the first book of the Holy Bible?
questions.explanation: Genesis recounts the creation of the heavens and the earth, the fall of man, and the patriarchs of the covenant.

questions.question: Who were the first man and woman created by God according to the Book of Genesis?
questions.explanation: God formed Adam from the dust of the ground and breathed into him the breath of life, and created Eve as his suitable partner.

questions.question: Whom did God command to build an ark of gopher wood to preserve his household and the living creatures from the deluge?
questions.explanation: Noah was found righteous in his generation and obeyed God in constructing the Ark.

questions.question: How long did rain pour upon the earth during the great flood in the days of Noah?
questions.explanation: Rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights, inaugurating the great flood.

questions.question: What celestial sign did God set in the clouds as a perpetual covenant that waters would never again destroy all flesh?
questions.explanation: God stated: 'I will set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be the sign of a covenant between me, and between the earth.'

questions.question: What city's inhabitants attempted to construct a tower reaching the heavens, resulting in the confusion of human speech?
questions.explanation: At the Tower of Babel, human pride sought to make a name for themselves, and the Lord confused their single language.

questions.question: Who answered God's call to leave his fatherland of Ur to become the father of a multitude of nations?
questions.explanation: God promised Abraham that in him and his seed all the families of the earth would be blessed.

questions.question: Which beloved son did Abraham bind upon Mount Moriah in faithful obedience to God's testing?
questions.explanation: The Akedah (binding of Isaac) prefigures God the Father offering His only-begotten Son on Calvary.

questions.question: Which son of Jacob was stripped of his tunic of many colors, sold into Egyptian bondage, and later became viceroy of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Joseph forgave his brothers, testifying: 'You thought evil against me: but God turned it into good.'

questions.question: Out of what miraculous sign did the Lord speak to Moses on Mount Horeb, commanding him to deliver Israel?
options: A burning bush that was not consumed
questions.explanation: The Angel of the Lord appeared in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush that burned without being consumed.

questions.question: How many plagues did God send upon Egypt to compel Pharaoh to release the children of Israel?
questions.explanation: The ten plagues culminated in the tenth plague on the firstborn, initiating the Passover.

questions.question: Which body of water did Moses part with his rod, allowing the Israelites to walk through on dry seabed?
questions.explanation: The Lord drove back the sea with a strong east wind all night, creating walls of water on their right and left.

questions.question: What molten idol did Aaron fashion at the demand of the Israelites while Moses was atop Sinai?
questions.explanation: Aaron fashioned a molten calf, prompting Moses to shatter the stone tablets upon descending the mountain.

questions.question: Who succeeded Moses as commander of Israel and led the twelve tribes across the Jordan into the Promised Land?
questions.explanation: God charged Joshua: 'Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee.'

questions.question: Which fortified Canaanite city had its walls collapse after the Israelites marched around it for seven days blowing ram's horns?
questions.explanation: On the seventh day, after seven circuits, the priests blew trumpets, the people shouted, and the walls fell flat.

questions.question: Which prophetess and judge of Israel sat under a palm tree in Ephraim and inspired Barak to overthrow Sisera?
questions.explanation: Deborah judged Israel at that time and accompanied the army of Mount Tabor to victory.

questions.question: Which judge of Israel possessed extraordinary supernatural strength bound to his consecrated Nazirite locks?
questions.explanation: Samson was consecrated to God as a Nazirite from the womb; no razor had ever touched his head.

questions.question: Who enticed Samson into revealing that his strength lay in his uncut hair, delivering him to the Philistines?
questions.explanation: Delilah coaxed Samson into confiding his secret and called a man to shave off the seven locks of his head.

questions.question: Which Moabite widow demonstrated profound devotion to her mother-in-law Naomi, proclaiming: 'Thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God'?
questions.explanation: Ruth married Boaz in Bethlehem and became the great-grandmother of King David, included in Christ's genealogy.

questions.question: Which young boy ministering before the High Priest Eli in Shiloh responded to God's nighttime voice: 'Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth'?
questions.explanation: The Lord revealed Himself to Samuel in Shiloh, establishing him as an accredited prophet to all Israel.

questions.question: Who was anointed by Samuel as the very first earthly king over the united tribes of Israel?
questions.explanation: Samuel took a vial of oil and poured it upon Saul's head, anointing him as captain over the Lord's inheritance.

questions.question: What Philistine giant from Gath did the young shepherd David strike down with a single sling stone?
questions.explanation: David confronted Goliath in the name of the Lord of Hosts, striking his forehead with a smooth brook stone.

questions.question: Which king of Israel established Jerusalem as his royal capital, composed numerous Psalms, and received God's eternal covenant promise?
questions.explanation: God promised David that his royal throne would be established forever, fulfilled eternally in Jesus the Son of David.

questions.question: Which son of David was gifted with unparalleled divine wisdom and erected the first Temple of the Lord in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: King Solomon asked God for an understanding heart to judge the people, and constructed the magnificent Temple on Mount Moriah.

questions.question: Which prophet challenged 450 prophets of Baal to a contest of fire on Mount Carmel, calling down divine fire from heaven?
questions.explanation: The fire of the Lord fell, consuming Elijah's sacrifice, wood, stones, and water in the trench.

questions.question: How was the prophet Elijah bodily assumed into the heavens in the presence of his disciple Elisha?
options: In a whirlwind with a chariot and horses of fire
questions.explanation: A chariot of fire and horses of fire parted them asunder, and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

questions.question: Which Syrian military commander was cured of leprosy after Elisha told him to wash seven times in the Jordan River?
questions.explanation: Naaman dipped seven times in the Jordan, and his flesh was restored like that of a little child.

questions.question: Which righteous Hebrew youth in Babylon interpreted Nebuchadnezzar's dreams and survived unhurt in a den of hungry lions?
questions.explanation: Daniel testified to King Darius: 'My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut up the mouths of the lions.'

questions.question: What were the Hebrew names of the three youths who were cast into the fiery furnace for refusing to worship the golden colossus?
options: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (Hananiah, Mishael, Azariah)
questions.explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar beheld a fourth figure walking with them unbound in the furnace, having the appearance of a son of God.

questions.question: Which reluctant prophet fled towards Tarshish on a ship, was swallowed by a great sea monster, and preached repentance to Nineveh?
questions.explanation: Jesus cited the 'sign of Jonah'—three days and nights in the whale's belly—as a typology for His resurrection.

questions.question: In which Judean city of David was Jesus Christ born in a manger, as foretold by the prophet Micah?
questions.explanation: Joseph and Mary journeyed to Bethlehem Ephrathah, the ancestral city of David, where Mary gave birth to Jesus.

questions.question: Which archangel was dispatched by God to Nazareth to announce the Incarnation to the Blessed Virgin Mary?
questions.explanation: Gabriel greeted Mary: 'Hail, full of grace, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.'

questions.question: Who lived in the wilderness clothed in camel's hair, baptizing with water and heralding: 'Behold the Lamb of God'?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist was the voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord.

questions.question: At which Galilean wedding feast did Jesus perform His first public miracle at the intercession of His Mother?
questions.explanation: At Mary's word ('Do whatever he tells you'), Jesus transformed six stone water jars of water into choice wine.

questions.question: How many Apostles did Jesus specially choose and commission to be the foundations of His Church?
questions.explanation: The Twelve Apostles correspond typologically to the twelve patriarchs of the twelve tribes of Israel.

questions.question: To which Apostle did Jesus say at Caesarea Philippi: 'Thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church'?
questions.explanation: Christ gave Peter the Keys of the Kingdom of Heaven and the power to bind and loose on earth.

questions.question: Which Apostle betrayed Jesus to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver in the Garden of Gethsemane?
questions.explanation: Judas betrayed the Lord with a kiss in Gethsemane, fulfilling Zechariah's prophecy regarding the thirty pieces of silver.

questions.question: How many times did Simon Peter deny knowing Jesus in the High Priest's courtyard before the cock crew?
questions.explanation: Peter denied Him thrice; immediately the cock crew, the Lord turned and looked at Peter, and Peter wept bitterly.

questions.question: What Roman procurator of Judea sentenced Jesus to be scourged and crucified after washing his own hands?
questions.explanation: Pilate took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying: 'I am innocent of the blood of this just person.'

questions.question: What is the name of the skull-shaped hill outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified between two thieves?
questions.explanation: Golgotha (Aramaic for 'the place of a skull', Latin: Calvaria) was the site of the holy cross.

questions.question: Who was the first person to encounter the risen Lord outside the empty garden tomb on Easter morning?
questions.explanation: The Risen Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, commissioning her as the 'apostle to the apostles'.

questions.question: Which Apostle doubted the Resurrection until Jesus invited him to put his finger into His nail-prints and side?
questions.explanation: Thomas exclaimed the great confession of divinity: 'My Lord and my God!' (Dominus meus et Deus meus).

questions.question: Who is honored in the Acts of the Apostles as the first Christian martyr (protomartyr), stoned while praying for his killers?
questions.explanation: Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked steadfastly into heaven, saw the glory of God, and prayed: 'Lord, lay not this sin to their charge.'

questions.question: On the road to which Syrian city was the persecutor Saul blinded by a blazing light from heaven and converted by the Risen Christ?
questions.explanation: Jesus called out: 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?' He was baptized by Ananias in Damascus and became St. Paul.

questions.question: How many total books are in the canonical New Testament accepted by the Church?
questions.citation: Council of Rome (382), Council of Trent (1546), CCC 120
questions.explanation: The New Testament canon comprises 27 books: four Gospels, Acts, fourteen Pauline Epistles (with Hebrews), seven Catholic Epistles, and Revelation.

questions.question: Which Apostle authored the Book of Revelation (Apocalypse) while exiled on the Greek island of Patmos?
questions.explanation: St. John was in the island called Patmos for the word of God, where he received the prophetic visions of the heavenly liturgy and New Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which two Evangelists were members of the original Twelve Apostles chosen by Jesus?
questions.explanation: St. Matthew (Levi the tax collector) and St. John (the beloved disciple) were eyewitness Apostles.

questions.question: Which famous Gospel discourse (Matthew 5–7) opens with the Eight Beatitudes: 'Blessed are the poor in spirit'?
questions.explanation: In the Sermon on the Mount, Christ promulgates the New Law of interior righteousness and divine beatitude.

questions.question: What did Jesus declare in Matthew 7:12: 'All things therefore whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them'?
questions.explanation: Jesus designated this ethical precept as the summation of the Law and the Prophets.

questions.question: When asked which is the great commandment in the Law, what did Jesus cite first?
options: Thou shalt honor thy father and mother
Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart, soul, and mind
Thou shalt keep the Sabbath holy
questions.explanation: Jesus answered with the Shema from Deuteronomy: to love God with all one's heart, soul, and mind; the second is like it: to love one's neighbor as oneself.

questions.question: In Ephesians 6, St. Paul describes the spiritual Armor of God. What is identified as the 'Sword of the Spirit'?
questions.explanation: St. Paul writes: 'And take unto you the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit (which is the word of God).'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 13:13, which three virtues remain, and which one does St. Paul declare is the greatest?
options: Faith, Hope, and Charity; the greatest is Charity (Love)
Justice, Wisdom, and Peace; the greatest is Peace
Humility, Patience, and Faith; the greatest is Faith
Prudence, Fortitude, and Temperance; the greatest is Fortitude
questions.explanation: 'And now there remain faith, hope, and charity, these three: but the greatest of these is charity.' Faith and hope pass away in heaven, but love endures eternally.

questions.question: In Galatians 5:22-23, what are listed as fruits of the Holy Spirit?
options: Love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control
questions.explanation: The fruits of the Spirit are perfections that the Holy Spirit forms in us as the first fruits of eternal glory.

questions.question: With what meager provision did Jesus miraculously feed the five thousand men beside the Sea of Galilee?
options: Seven loaves and a few small fish
Five barley loaves and two fish
Three loaves of wheat and oil
A bowl of lentils and figs
questions.explanation: A young boy had five barley loaves and two fishes; Jesus blessed them, broke them, and twelve baskets of fragments were gathered.

questions.question: Which two Old Testament figures appeared in radiant glory conversing with Jesus on the Mount of Transfiguration?
questions.explanation: Moses (representing the Law) and Elijah (representing the Prophets) appeared speaking of His departure (exodus) in Jerusalem.

questions.question: In John 10, what title does Jesus bestow upon Himself, contrasting with the hireling who flees when the wolf attacks?
questions.explanation: 'I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd giveth his life for his sheep.'

questions.question: In the Bread of Life discourse (John 6), what solemn declaration does Christ make regarding His flesh?
options: My flesh is meat indeed: and my blood is drink indeed
My flesh is merely a symbol of brotherhood
My flesh shall be remembered in spirit only
My flesh is like manna that perished in the desert
questions.explanation: 'He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, abideth in me, and I in him.'

questions.question: In which Gospel does Jesus teach His disciples the 'Our Father' (Pater Noster) during the Sermon on the Mount?
questions.explanation: The Lord's Prayer is the quintessential Christian prayer taught by the Master Himself.

questions.question: What humble act of servanthood did Jesus perform for His disciples before instituting the Eucharist at the Last Supper?
options: He crowned them with olive wreaths
He anointed their heads with nard
He bestowed golden garments upon them
questions.explanation: Jesus poured water into a basin and washed the disciples' feet, commanding them to do as He had done.

questions.question: From which mount near Jerusalem did the Risen Lord ascend into heaven forty days after His resurrection?
questions.explanation: He was taken up in a cloud from the Mount of Olives while the Apostles watched, and two angels promised His return in like manner.

questions.question: What kind of tree did the short tax collector Zacchaeus climb in Jericho in order to see Jesus pass by?
questions.explanation: Zacchaeus ran before and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see Him, and Jesus lodged at his home that day.

questions.question: For how many days had Lazarus of Bethany been buried in the tomb before Jesus cried out: 'Lazarus, come forth'?
questions.explanation: Martha noted that he had been in the tomb four days, yet Jesus commanded the stone rolled away and raised him to life.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son (Luke 15), what did the compassionate father order his servants to bring for the returning younger son?
options: The best robe, a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet
A bag of coins to repay the debt
questions.explanation: The father welcomed his repentant son with the best robe, a signet ring, sandals, and killed the fatted calf for celebration.

questions.question: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep, how many sheep did the shepherd leave in the wilderness to search for the single one that went astray?
questions.explanation: The shepherd leaves the ninety-nine in the desert and goes after the one that was lost until he finds it.

questions.question: To which Pharisee and ruler of the Jews did Jesus say: 'Amen, amen I say to thee, unless a man be born again of water and the Holy Ghost, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God'?
questions.explanation: Nicodemus came to Jesus by night, and Jesus revealed the necessity of spiritual regeneration through Baptism.

questions.question: In the Great Commission (Matthew 28:19), in whose Name did the Risen Christ command His Apostles to baptize all nations?
options: In the name of Jesus only
In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost
In the name of Abraham and Moses
In the name of the Holy Catholic Church
questions.explanation: 'Going therefore, teach ye all nations; baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.'

questions.question: At whose ancestral well in Sychar did Jesus converse with the Samaritan woman, offering her 'living water'?
questions.explanation: Jacob's well was there; Jesus, tired from his journey, sat by the well and revealed Himself as the Messiah.

questions.question: Which Apostle climbed out of the fishing boat to walk on the stormy waves of the Sea of Galilee toward Jesus?
questions.explanation: Peter walked on the water, but seeing the wind strong, became afraid and began to sink, crying: 'Lord, save me!'

questions.question: Which three Apostles accompanied Jesus to witness His Transfiguration and later His Agony in Gethsemane?
options: Jude, James the Less, and Matthias
questions.explanation: Peter, James, and John formed the intimate inner circle of the Apostles chosen to witness Christ's greatest glories and trials.

questions.question: On which Mediterranean island was St. Paul shipwrecked while being transported under Roman guard to appeal to Caesar?
questions.explanation: All 276 passengers escaped safely to shore on Malta, where Paul shook off a venomous viper without harm.

questions.question: Which judge of Israel reduced his army from thirty-two thousand men down to three hundred who lapped water with their tongues?
questions.explanation: The Lord told Gideon that with the three hundred men who lapped water he would deliver Midian, proving that salvation belongs to God.

questions.question: Which Jewish queen risked her life before Persian King Ahasuerus to thwart Haman's plot to exterminate her people?
questions.explanation: Esther fasted three days and approached the king, declaring: 'If I perish, I perish', rescuing her people and establishing Purim.

questions.question: Which major prophet beheld the Lord high and lifted up, while Seraphim cried 'Holy, Holy, Holy' (Sanctus)?
questions.explanation: Isaiah saw the Lord seated upon a throne, and a Seraph touched his mouth with a live coal, purging his iniquity.

questions.question: In which chapter of Isaiah is the Messiah foretold as the Suffering Servant who 'was wounded for our iniquities, bruised for our sins'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53 provides the profound prophecy of the Passion of Christ, led like a lamb to the slaughter.

questions.question: Which righteous man from the land of Uz endured the loss of his children, wealth, and health yet declared: 'The Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord'?
questions.explanation: Job maintained his integrity and faith in the Redeemer: 'I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth.'

questions.question: Which deuterocanonical book describes the young man Tobias guided on his perilous journey by the Archangel Raphael?
questions.explanation: The Archangel Raphael revealed himself: 'I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven, who stand before the Lord.'

questions.question: Which books of the Catholic Old Testament recount the heroic revolt led by Judas Maccabeus against Antiochus IV Epiphanes to rededicate the Temple?
questions.explanation: The Maccabees cleansed the sanctuary and instituted the eight-day Feast of the Dedication of the Altar.

questions.question: In 2 Maccabees 12:46, what salutary practice is affirmed as holy and wholesome?
options: Praying and making atonement for the dead that they may be loosed from their sins
questions.explanation: 'It is therefore a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead, that they may be loosed from sins'—a foundational scriptural support for Purgatory.

questions.question: Which courageous Jewish widow decapitated the Assyrian general Holofernes in his tent, delivering Bethulia and all Israel?
questions.explanation: Judith prayed for divine strength, struck Holofernes twice on his neck, and carried his head back to Bethulia.

questions.question: Which three Gospels are known as the 'Synoptic Gospels' due to their shared perspective and common outline of Christ's ministry?
questions.explanation: Matthew, Mark, and Luke can be viewed 'with one eye' (synoptic) because of their chronological and narrative parallels.

questions.question: Which Evangelist, companion of St. Paul and physician by trade, also authored the Book of the Acts of the Apostles?
questions.explanation: St. Luke ('the beloved physician') addressed both his Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles to the honorable Theophilus.

questions.question: What did the penitent thief (St. Dismas) say to Jesus on the cross, receiving the promise: 'This day thou shalt be with me in paradise'?
options: Lord, remember me when thou shalt come into thy kingdom
If thou be the Christ, save thyself and us
Master, tell my brother to divide the inheritance
Have mercy on me, a poor sinner from Galilee
questions.explanation: Dismas rebuked the other criminal, confessed Jesus' innocence, and asked to be remembered in His Kingdom.

questions.question: From which royal lineage and house was St. Joseph, the chaste spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary and foster father of Jesus?
questions.explanation: The angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying: 'Joseph, son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife.'

questions.question: Who leaped with joy in the womb of St. Elizabeth when the pregnant Virgin Mary greeted her at the Visitation?
questions.explanation: Elizabeth exclaimed: 'For behold as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy.'

questions.question: Which majestic canticle did the Virgin Mary proclaim at the home of Elizabeth, opening: 'My soul doth magnify the Lord'?
questions.explanation: The Magnificat is Mary's song of thanksgiving praising God for exalting the humble and scattering the proud.

questions.question: Which elder priest and father of John the Baptist had his speech restored and proclaimed the 'Benedictus' canticle?
questions.explanation: Zechariah wrote 'John is his name', his tongue was loosed, and he prophesied: 'Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people.'

questions.question: In which Epistle did St. Paul write the celebrated Christological hymn describing Christ emptying Himself ('Kenosis') and taking the form of a servant?
questions.explanation: Christ 'emptied himself, taking the form of a servant... wherefore God also hath exalted him, and given him a name which is above all names.'

questions.question: What is the Hebrew/Aramaic word meaning 'Amen, Come Lord Jesus' used by early Christians and St. Paul in 1 Cor 16:22?
questions.explanation: 'Maranatha' is the ancient liturgical invocation meaning 'Our Lord, come!' expressing fervent longing for the Parousia.

questions.question: With what benediction does the entire Sacred Scripture conclude in Revelation 22:21?
options: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen
Woe to the inhabitants of the earth
Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord God of hosts
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost
questions.explanation: The Bible closes with St. John's loving benediction of the grace of Jesus Christ upon all the faithful.
